Most of its work fits that role: it chooses data providers, validates activities, merges search results, derives currency quotes and calls other services. But `getHistorical` writes and runs its own SQL. It builds `Prisma.sql` fragments using the Postgres functions `date_part` and `TIMESTAMP 'yesterday'`, then runs `prismaService.$queryRaw` with a `SELECT * FROM "MarketData"` query. It also maps the raw rows into the response itself. Query building, SQL and table access belong in the infrastructure layer (a repository), or behind `MarketDataService`, which this class already injects. Other parts are weaker concerns: `getQuotes` reads and writes cache entries with `JSON.parse` and `JSON.stringify` and builds the cache keys itself. That leans toward infrastructure, but an application service can reasonably decide when to use a cache, so it is not reported as a violation. The raw SQL alone is enough to fail the unit.
